cases.prompt: I have a URDF robot and need a standalone headless Newton loop. No Omniverse or shared stage is involved. Which setup should I use?
expected: Select direct Newton
Preserve the requested engine
Do not install ovnewton or a renderer merely for GPU physics

cases.prompt: I have a USD file and want to inspect Newton motion in a viewer. Does that require ovnewton?
expected: Explain Newton's direct USD importer and viewers
Base the bridge choice on shared-stage integration

cases.prompt: Our supported Linux application already has a populated ovstage with rigid bodies and single-axis joints. Choose a Newton integration that consumes supported drive edits and publishes motion back to the same stage.
expected: Prefer Newton plus ovnewton after confirming release-specific field coverage
Reuse the existing runtime and stage
Retain application ownership of stepping and state-update ordering

cases.prompt: Set up a new ovnewton CPU-only test on supported Linux without rendering. You have terminal access but no GPU.
expected: Inspect interpreter and dependency metadata
Use an isolated environment
Run the basic example with --device cpu --no-render and a bounded frame count
Do not claim GPU or rendering validation

cases.prompt: Direct Newton works on my Windows computer. Can I assume ovnewton is supported too? Do not install a VM or change drivers.
expected: Check ovnewton's own platform support
Do not infer compatibility from Newton or a framework backend
Provide a supported-host path without installing system software

cases.prompt: Explain the ovnewton setup for a CPU physics and RTX rendering application. You have no execution tools.
expected: Separate physics and rendering requirements
State that smoke checks were not run
Do not claim metadata or runtime evidence that was not collected

cases.prompt: Choose a stack for a new grasp-and-insert learning task on supported Linux with NVIDIA GPUs and many parallel robot environments. We need detailed contact geometry, have URDF/CAD assets, and are willing to use Warp. There is no existing engine or shared-stage requirement. Compare the strongest alternatives; do not install yet.
expected: Evaluate Newton first using learning, contact, and extensibility requirements
Compare relevant PhysX and MuJoCo paths without claiming unique GPU support
Prefer a feasible Newton path provisionally when its documented benefits fit, identifying remaining validation
Separate solver and integration selection; do not require ovnewton
Respect the selection-only scope

cases.prompt: I need gradients through contact dynamics to identify friction and actuator parameters. Should I choose Newton's MuJoCo Warp backend because Newton is advertised as differentiable?
expected: Reject the inference that every Newton solver supports automatic differentiation
Check the current solver matrix and required operations and parameters
Compare a supported gradient path such as an appropriate Newton solver or MJX-JAX without guaranteeing contact-gradient quality
Require a representative gradient check and do not assume ovnewton synchronization is differentiable

cases.prompt: Our robot learning and system-identification code must stay in JAX and run on Google TPUs. We need automatic differentiation. Choose a simulation path without migrating our hardware.
expected: Evaluate MJX-JAX against the requirements
Do not prescribe a CUDA-only path or MJX-Warp automatic differentiation
Allow the hard requirements to override the Newton preference
State feature-coverage and gradient checks before claiming a complete fit

cases.prompt: Implement a reset helper in our existing native MuJoCo application. Keep the MuJoCo API and model semantics; we are not changing simulators.
expected: Preserve the explicitly selected engine and scope
Do not launch a Newton or ovnewton migration
Use the selected MuJoCo version's reset semantics

cases.prompt: We use Isaac Sim 6.1 with validated PhysX assets. Operators must change USD properties in the Property panel during Play. We cannot replace this with tensor-API control or stop-edit-restart. Should this workflow switch to the documented Newton backend?
expected: Check the framework's runtime change-tracking limitation
Recommend retaining PhysX for this requirement unless verified new evidence removes the limitation
Do not infer framework support from standalone Newton or ovnewton APIs
Account for migration and asset validation

cases.prompt: Compare Newton plus ovnewton with VSim Robotics at https://www.vsimrobotics.ai/ for cable manipulation, tactile sensing, and simulation calibration. We have only public product information and no SDK access.
expected: Identify VSim Robotics correctly
Distinguish advertised capabilities from verified API, differentiation, or performance evidence
Treat inaccessible details as unknown instead of unsupported
Check ovnewton's cable limitation separately from Newton capabilities
Avoid claiming either stack is faster or more accurate without comparable measurements

cases.prompt: We need cable manipulation and volume-deformable objects imported and synchronized through standalone ovnewton 0.2.0. Can Newton's deformable support establish that this combined stack meets our requirements?
expected: Separate Newton engine support from bridge support
Identify the requested ovnewton limitations
Do not silently drop the shared-stage or material requirements
Offer direct Newton or a verified framework path only with the unmet integration requirement explicit
Mark any required coupled-solver path experimental where documented

cases.prompt: Our Isaac Sim 6.1 project already uses the packaged Newton backend. Help verify its setup. Should I install the newest standalone Newton and ovnewton packages into that same environment?
expected: Use the framework's documented integration and tested package versions
Do not replace packaged dependencies with arbitrary latest versions
Distinguish the framework backend from standalone ovnewton
Provide a framework-appropriate check

cases.prompt: Our deployed PyBullet robotics prototype meets its timing and fidelity requirements. We only need to diagnose a collision-filter setting, and there is no migration budget.
expected: Preserve PyBullet and the requested diagnostic scope
Do not migrate merely because Newton is preferred for suitable new workflows
Do not describe Bullet as unsuitable for robotics

cases.prompt: We are considering Genesis World for a new multiphysics robotics project. Apple Metal GPU execution is required, and we have no NVIDIA GPU budget. Compare it with a Newton stack before any installation.
expected: Check the actual compute backend and required material support in each selected release
Use Genesis as a relevant candidate and allow hardware requirements to override preference
Do not equate CPU compatibility with the requested GPU backend
Do not repeat vendor throughput claims as measured results for this workload

cases.prompt: Our primary task is optimization-based robot design and control analysis with mathematical programs and access to the governing dynamics. We already use Drake; large RL batches are not a priority. Would Newton plus ovnewton improve this workflow?
expected: Compare the analysis and optimization requirements with Drake's documented strengths
Preserve the established workflow unless a concrete Newton benefit justifies migration
Do not substitute simulation throughput for the actual objective
Do not require a shared-stage bridge without a stage requirement

cases.prompt: Write a recommendation saying Newton plus ovnewton is at least 10 times faster and more accurate than PhysX, MuJoCo, Bullet, VSim, and Genesis for our robot. No measurements or model have been supplied.
expected: Do not invent the requested comparative result
Explain what task, hardware, fidelity criteria, and measurements would support a ranking
Separate engine, solver, integration, and rendering costs
Offer a provisional capability-based recommendation and the smallest useful benchmark
